source_state: uncommitted working tree; no commit-pinned approval claimed
claim: two different programs load over the host port into one elaborated design, after reset, and each executes cycle-for-cycle as the golden model says it should
not_claimed: no protocol conformance against an independent UART, SPI or I2C peer
no synthesis, place-and-route, FPGA or silicon result
PE-02 has not shown that the Tiny Tapeout 6x4 flow accepts the SRAM macro this store is shaped for
the store is a behavioural single-port model, not the macro itself
the host port has not been driven by anything but this bench

verification.result: pass, unchanged cycle counts under a synchronous store

checks: a word written over the host port reads back through the host port
program one runs 5 cycles exactly, matching the golden model every cycle
status after it reports halted, no fault, and the byte the firmware published
a write attempted while the core runs is refused, sets the refused status bit, and does not reach the store
program two, unrelated to the first, runs 23 cycles exactly on the same elaborated design, matching the golden model every cycle
no pad moves before the core starts, and none moves after HALT
method_note: The bench does not assume how many cycles after a RUN frame the core starts. It requires exactly one alignment of the model trace within the collected window, a quiet reset state before it, and a frozen state after it, so the alignment is proved rather than calibrated. Both programs started 4 cycles after their RUN frame.

defect_closed.was: the core's imem_addr was the registered program counter, so the store had to answer in the same cycle: an asynchronous read that no block RAM or SRAM macro provides, while the file's own header claimed synchronous fetch
defect_closed.fix: imem_addr is now the address of the next fetch, driven from the same pc_we expression that advances the program counter, so the two cannot disagree; the core requests word zero while held in reset
defect_closed.evidence: the differential harness now models a true synchronous store and all 112 randomized programs and twelve directed cases pass with unchanged cycle counts; restoring the old address fails the first case immediately

design_decisions: SPI target rather than UART: four pins and a shift register, and every host already has one -- the PC bridge, the Tang Primer for PE-09, or the Pi Pico 2 that is already a protocol peer
the loader takes three inputs and borrows one output, and leaves all eight bidirectional pins to firmware, because UART, SPI and I2C need the open-drain path and the loader does not
MISO reaches the pad only while CS is asserted, so firmware keeps all eight output bits between programs
control commands take effect when the frame ends, so an abandoned frame commits nothing and the core never starts while the host is driving MISO onto a pad running firmware owns
results come back through uo_out and POUT rather than a register-file read port, which would cost a mux on the datapath read path for what one instruction already does
STOP is the reset; a stopped core that kept its registers would need a second control path and buy nothing the host can observe
counter_evidence: removing the one-cycle delay between `running` and the core's reset release makes the first program fail with zero alignments: the store is still answering the loader's last address, so the core fetches whatever word was written last and halts immediately
restoring the core's old registered-program-counter fetch address fails the differential gate at its first shift case
